tests.name: Effective description
tests.message: Verdict not allowed for this test: 'warning' (allowed: passed, failed)

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what a model registry is, what SageMaker is) and jumps directly into domain-specific check-ids, routing logic, and governance procedures that are specific to this skill's domain.
tests.evidence: 'Grounded in checks-sagemaker-model-registry.md; load it when a symptom matches a row below. Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed material (full detection rules, remediations, citations, API quirks, metrics) in reference files and only includes a compact summary table in the body, with explicit pointers to load details conditionally.
tests.evidence: 'The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-model-registry.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, known-causes.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific trigger condition explaining when to load it, rather than a generic 'see for details' mention.
tests.evidence: 'load it before assigning any check-id or severity' and 'load it whenever the user names an error or symptom'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, validation checklist, severity rules) are highly prescriptive with exact rules, while flexible areas (break-fix triage, review procedure) explain purpose and allow judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: 'Never call a registry mutation (CreateModelPackage, UpdateModelPackage) or any other mutating API. Recommend the fix and give the exact CLI/IaC command; let the user run it.'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools/approaches as equal choices; instead it defines a clear deterministic sequence (first read, then load) per symptom in the Router table.
tests.evidence: '| Operator says | First read | Load |' table rows specify a single first API call per symptom, not multiple equal options.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable approach (match symptom to check, confirm via API, report with check-id and severity) rather than a one-off instance-specific declaration.
tests.evidence: 'Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a 'Common wrong answers' section and an 'Error Handling' section documenting specific non-obvious pitfalls (e.g., approved package vs deployed version, CloudWatch no-datapoints trap).
tests.evidence: '"There is an `Approved` package in the group, so the group is governed." Approval only counts for the version that is actually deployed or staged.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides a report template in assets/ for structured output, consistent with its review/report-generating purpose.
tests.evidence: 'Use [model-registry-health-report-template.md](assets/model-registry-health-report-template.md) when a full report is requested'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body

tests.name: Asset files must be linked

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load

tests.name: Asset path format
